limits.35: 35. Disclosure: while building the evaluation core, one builder's look at a temp file showed the names of files in two held-out commits (dated 2026-08-03). No truth was computed or used from it; tuning truth came from git for the June commits only. The audit records it.
limits.39: 39. Stage A's held-out set is small: the stage-A graph has 162 co_changed pairs, so 16 pairs (32 queries) are held out. Its top-3 filter is noisy; the binding selection is stage B's nested task-level choice. Reported as a limit. Stage A is not restarted (its count, not its scores, prompted this).
limits.43: 43. Item 2 reads: every training, scoring and smoke run uses `--network none`, `--cpus 6`, a memory cap of at most 4 GB (stage B and held-out: 2560m; 2g was the lowest cap that ran every arm), and `--gpus all` for card runs. One lane container at a time unless the coordinator rules otherwise under ruling 66; a container starts only when three samples 30 s apart show host free RAM of at least 4.5 GB and commit charge under 40 GB, and is stopped (its unit redone) after three samples under 2.5 GB free or over 43 GB commit (below the ship coordinator's own alarm at 2 GB / 44 GB). Stage B and held-out keep at most 5 GB on disk. A run's model file is deleted once its scores are written and read back. The representation file ruling 61 keeps per arm is stage A's (CPU; `train/stageA/<arm>/<config>/reps.pt`).
limits.44: 44. Stride. s (item 16, ruling 37) is set from the card's timing alone, by the same rule: the smallest of 1, 3, 6, 10 whose projected stage B is under 30 hours, else 10. Value: s = 1, from the card's timing of the selected configurations at ruling 36's epochs (`gpu/stride-gpu-lanes1.json`): projected 14.4 h with one training process (s = 3: 4.8 h; 6: 2.3 h; 10: 1.6 h); 53 tuning checkpoints, 2,385 units, lag 0 for all 388 tasks. No task score was read. On the CPU, ruling 37's projection was not redone after stage A. The CPU timing before stage A gave 375 to 1,464 hours at s = 1 and 41 to 159 hours at s = 10 (`train/stride.json`), so on the CPU no stride fitted 30 hours and s would have been 10 under ruling 37. The card therefore sets s, and with it the lag of ruling 38 (0 for every task). Rulings 49-52 and item 17's fold-in do not act at s = 1 (rulings 48 and 65). The s > 1 rows predate rulings 49-51 (the plan gives 19, 10 and 7 checkpoints); they do not change s. The number of processes follows ruling 66 (one by default; two or three in one container reached the 4 GB cap, an E4 process was killed at three, for a gain of 1.3 to 1.66 times).
limits.45: 45. Item 29's "GPUs" limit now reads: "the card was used to shorten wall time, and that allowed s = 1, so every stage-B embedding is trained at the task's own parent (ruling 44); large dimensions and card-scale models were still not tested".
limits.46: 46. Nondeterminism. Card kernels may differ from run to run, and floating-point sums differ from the CPU's. Before any card timing was trusted, three checks ran. The shared checks passed on the card. Scores of one trained model agreed between CPU and card within 1.6e-5 on 20 queries per arm, top 10 identical 20 of 20. Each arm's stage-A best configuration was retrained on the card with stage A's split and seed; validation MRR, CPU to card: E1 0.730/0.730, E2 0.752/0.752, E3 0.741/0.723 (same best epoch, 32 queries), E5 0.402/0.401. E4 gave 0.209 under the patience rule and 0.555 at its peak without it, before ruling 42's initialisation fix. After the fix, at a fixed 95 epochs, seeds 1-3: CPU 0.729, 0.657, 0.596 (mean 0.661), card 0.704, 0.648, 0.698 (mean 0.683), read as seed and trajectory variance. These are sanity checks, never a selection input. Seeds are reported per run; a rerun on the card may differ, at validation level by a few hundredths on 32 queries.
limits.47: 47. When the choice was made: the owner approved the card at 08:35Z on 2026-11-14, with 76 of 80 stage-A units finished (E5 c13-c16, none later in E5's top 3, still running); this section was written after stage A finished. Stage A's selection scores (validation MRR on its held-out pairs; they decide only which three configurations go on, item 19) had been seen. No stage-B unit and no task-level embedding score existed then or when this section was accepted. The device was chosen for wall time, and s from the card's timing alone (ruling 44), not from any score. Disclosed: E4's initialisation fix (ruling 42) followed the card sanity runs that showed E4 at 0.209 and 0.555. The fix was kept because it makes E4's initial weights bit-identical to the CPU's, which variant A did not. The validation MRRs of both variants (means 0.626 and 0.683; CPU 0.661) were seen before it was kept.
limits.67: 67. Deterministic E4. Every stage-B and held-out E4 unit (c12, c13, c16; seeds 1 to 3; every checkpoint, every redo and every reference run) trains with PyTorch's deterministic algorithms (`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`, warn_only off) and `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8`. Reason, measured on the card on 2026-11-14: without them E4 gives different losses from epoch 1 and different score tables on two runs alone, so no E4 result could ever be checked by a re-run; with them E4 repeats byte for byte alone and beside another container, at 8 to 20 % more seconds per epoch. The model, its settings, seeds and data are unchanged; only the order of additions on the card is fixed. The flags are set by a launcher wrapper, not in hashed code; every E4 part records them in its runner field, and assemble refuses an E4 part without them. If a deterministic kernel is missing for c13 or c16, E4 runs in its earlier form, alone, and that is reported with the result.
limits.68: 68. What "unchanged" means when units run side by side (ruling 66). For E1, E2, E3 and deterministic E4: byte-identity of the loss list, every representation tensor, both score tables and the counts, against the same unit trained alone. For E5: identical score tables and counts. E5's representations and losses drift in the last bit from about epoch 29 on some graphs even when it trains alone (four alone runs all differed; the score tables were identical in all ten runs), so byte-identity of its representations cannot be shown for it alone or side by side. Reported as a limit: E5 is not bit-reproducible on the card. A setting that turns out not to repeat alone is held to E5's criterion and named in the result.
limits.96c: Ruling 96 (c), a difference between the splits: the held-out graphs carry a layer the tuning graphs lack, so the settings were chosen on graphs without it; they hold one relation type and two node kinds that no tuning checkpoint has, in 69 of the 70 parents (37 relation types against 36). Ruling 99, a correction: Rulings 96 and 97 give the relation types as "37 against 36". The right figures are 36 against 35, the changed-together relation included in both: the tuning checkpoints hold 35 relation types between them, the held-out parents 36 (69 graphs hold 36 and one holds 35), and the largest held-out graph holds 36, as its size file says.
97: Ruling 97 (b), E5's routing on held-out: a file seed tied to the new nodes can get the `other` specialist as its second one, and that specialist is skipped where it has no co_changed fact; This is item 13's rule applied to a graph with a new layer, not a defect. In this run: the frozen arm is E1, not E5: the counts are not computed.

Ruling 97 (d): On held-out the candidate pool and the simple rankers run on a file-collapsed graph in which the new nodes are merged into one non-code file node that links the files they point to. Pools on held-out are therefore wider, for every method alike; median pool size: late 50 39 (313 tasks), held-out 80.0 (418 tasks) (from the parts' and the stage-B counts).

Under ruling 97 (d), D1 (r58c/closed-lists/FINDINGS-common.md): On held-out, the PPR comparator and the PPR half of every fused variant walk through the new hub. Their orders, and with them what each budget packs, therefore change on graphs the settings never saw, alike for every arm's fused form.
limits.98: 98. The cap of the remaining stage-B units is 4 GB (item 2's maximum; ruling 43's 2560m is amended for them). Measured on 2026-11-15: the container ran E4 c12 (159 units) and the first 39 units of c13 in one process and was then killed by the kernel at the 2560m cap (exit 137) at 05:55:39Z; each relaunch since has finished exactly one unit and been killed about twenty seconds into the next (05:59:07Z, 06:02:32Z), because the process still holds the first model's memory when the second is built on the larger checkpoints. At one unit per launch the 279 units left would take about sixteen hours, and a launch that finished none would stop the guard. The cap changes no result: it limits memory, not arithmetic; E4 is deterministic (rulings 67 and 87), and the re-run check of the end order trains one c13 and one c16 unit again in a fresh process and compares them byte for byte with the parts made under either cap. The guard script is not edited: its cap is read from the environment, so the same file (sha256 59d3fb8e...) is started with the cap set to 4g, and its start line records it. The guard's memory and disk lines are unchanged. AUDIT.md lists which units ran under which cap, from the guard log, and the result's limits carry this ruling beside ruling 43. If the container is still killed under 4 GB, the lane reports and changes nothing further.
limits.item28: 28. One repository, about 233 commits of history, about 5,400 nodes and 19,000 edges: about 7 facts per entity. A null here says nothing about larger or denser graphs.
limits.item29: 29. Not tested: temporal knowledge-graph models, inductive models (NodePiece, NBFNet), text or code embeddings, GPUs and large dimensions, rule learners (AnyBURL), a longer history.
limits.item30: 30. The truth is what a commit changed, at file level; context a change needed but did not edit is not scored. No agent is run.
limits.item31: 31. With 50 evaluation commits the smallest detectable difference is several hundredths; "cannot tell" is a likely outcome and is reported as "no evidence either way at this size".
